INTEREST OF THE AMICA CURIAE1
Like the parents in this case, Amica Curiae  Erin
Lee is a victim of state-sponsored interference with
her parental rights. Mrs. Lee’s daughter, a minor, was
indoctrinated into radical gender ideology after being
lured to an after-school meeting by one of her teachers.
There, she was introduced to issues of gender and sexuality
without the knowledge or consent of her parents and was
encouraged to keep what she had learned a secret from
her parents. At the meeting, Mrs. Lee’s daughter, who had
never before exhibited gender confusion, announced that
she was transitioning her gender. Mrs. Lee sued the school
district for their actions and pursued her case vigorously
until being denied certiorari  by this Court. Lee v. Poudre
Sch. Dist. R-1, 146 S. Ct. 26 (2025). Since then, Mrs. Lee
has become a parental rights advocate through her work
with Protect Kids Colorado, fighting to protect children
from being victimized by state-sponsored gender ideology.
She has an interest in this case in seeing more children
protected from the harmful influences of radical gender
indoctrination and in seeing more parents be granted
legal standing to challenge the harm being done to their
children without their consent.
SUMMARY OF THE ARGUMENT
In Amica Curiae  Erin Lee’s case and in Parents
Protecting Our Children, UA v. Eau Claire Area School
1. No counsel for a party authored this brief, in whole or in
part, and no person or entity other than counsel for amica curiae

2
District , a total of four justices recognized the growing
national importance of state policies allowing minors to
transition their genders without parental consent. Justice
Alito also correctly predicted that many of these cases
will not reach a decision on the merits of this important
constitutional question because courts would prefer to
dismiss them on procedural grounds like lack of standing.
Lower courts have split on how to address parental
standing in the context of child gender transitions without
parental consent. Courts in at least three cases that
reached this Court found that the plaintiff parents lacked
standing. But courts in at least three other cases held
that the plaintiff parents had standing—or it was never
challenged. The Court should grant certiorari  in this
case to resolve the split among lower courts regarding
parental standing.
Only if it clarifies its parental standing doctrine will
this Court avoid more horror stories like Mrs. Lee’s.
Mrs. Lee and her husband were the victims of radical
gender ideology policies promoted by their children’s
public school. Mrs. Lee’s daughter was lured to an afterschool activity under false pretenses, where she was
introduced to and encouraged to adopt transgender and
queer identities. Much to the shame of the school district
that condoned these actions, Mrs. Lee’s daughter was
encouraged to keep what was discussed a secret from her
parents. State officials have no right to introduce children
to issues of gender and sexuality without the consent of
the child’s parents.
Yet the Washington law at issue in this case requires
state officials to facilitate gender transitioning of runaway

3
children without parental notice or consent. The plaintiff
association representing parents in this case includes four
sets of parents who have gender confused children whom
they would like to maintain identification with their sex
at birth. One set of parents even has a child who has run
away once and would be subjected to the Washington law
requiring gender confused children to receive gender
affirming treatment without the need for parental consent.
Therefore, this case represents an important opportunity
for the Court to clarify the question of who has parental
standing to protect children from state-sponsored, gender
transitions of minors without parental consent. For these
reasons, the Court should grant certiorari .
ARGUMENT
I.  The Court should clarify that parents have standing
to challenge states’ promotion of gender transitions
without parental consent.
The underlying issue of this case—whether a
state may facilitate a child’s gender transition without
parental consent—is one of “‘great and growing national
importance,’” Lee v. Poudre Sch. Dist. R-1 , 146 S. Ct.
26 (2025) (Alito, J., concurring in denial of certiorari ,
joined by Thomas, J., and Gorsuch, J.) (quoting Parents
Protecting Our Children , 145 S. Ct. at 14 (2024)) (Alito,
J., dissenting from denial of certiorari , joined by Thomas,
J.; Kavanaugh, J., also “would grant the petition for a
writ of certiorari ”). The underlying issue is also one on
which lower courts disagree. Compare Foote v. Ludlow
Sch. Comm., 128 F .4th 336 (1st Cir. 2025) and Littlejohn
v. Sch. Bd. of Leon Cnty., Fla. , 132 F .4th 1232 (11th Cir.
2025) with Mirabelli v. Olson, No. 3:23-cv-768-BEN-WVG,
2025 WL 3713588 (S.D. Cal. Dec. 22, 2025).

4
But a majority of courts, including the Ninth Circuit in
this case, are failing to reach this important issue because
they are misapplying this Court’s standing doctrine. They
are fulfilling Justice Alito’s prophetic words in dissent
from the denial of certiorari  in Parents Protecting Our
Children : “I am concerned that some federal courts
are succumbing to the temptation to use the doctrine of
Article III standing as a way of avoiding some particularly
contentious constitutional questions.” 145 S. Ct. 14. The
Court should take this case to provide clarity on parental
standing in gender transition cases, so courts will reach
the important underlying issue of gender transitioning a
child without parental consent.
Several cases have evaded reaching the merits of
hiding gender transitions from parents by denying
parental standing. In  John & Jane Parents 1 v.
Montgomery County Board of Education , parents of
public-school students brought suit alleging that the school
board’s guidelines for developing gender transition plans
violated parents’ rights by permitting implementation
without parental knowledge or consent. 78 F .4th 622, 626
(4th Cir. 2023), cert. denied , 144 S. Ct. 2560 (2024). But
the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals failed to rule on the
merits, instead dismissing the case for lack of standing. Id.
In Parents Protecting Our Children , the Seventh
Circuit, likewise, upheld a district court’s dismissal for
lack of standing. Parents Protecting Our Children, UA
v. Eau Claire Area Sch. Dist., 95 F .4th 501, 506 (7th Cir.),
cert. denied , 145 S. Ct. 14 (2024). There, the court denied
the plaintiffs associational standing on behalf of parents
who were challenging a similar public-school policy for
gender transitioning children without parental knowledge
or consent. Id.

5
Amica  E rin  L e e ,  h e rs e lf ,  w as  o ri gin all y  d e ni e d
standing as a parent for asserting some of her claims
challenging her school district’s promotion of gender
transition practices to her children without her consent.
Lee v. Poudre Sch. Dist. R-1 , No. 23-CV-01117-NYW-
STV, 2023 WL 8780860, at *7 (D. Colo. Dec. 19, 2023).
Ultimately, the Tenth Circuit dismissed Mrs. Lee’s case
on the alternative procedural ground that the municipality
did not bear liability for causing her harm. Lee v. Poudre
Sch. Dist. R-1 , 135 F .4th 924, 927 (10th Cir. 2025), cert.
denied, 146 S. Ct. 26 (2025).
On the other hand, several cases have assumed
parental standing or granted it to parents in cases
involving gender transitioning without parental consent.
In Foote v. Ludlow School Committee , 128 F .4th 336 (1st
Cir. 2025), cert. pending , No. 25-77, defendants did not
raise the issue that parents lacked standing to bring their
claim. There, the First Circuit reached the merits of the
question of whether schools can hide gender transitions
from parents, but it incorrectly held that the school
protocol was a matter of curriculum and therefore not
subject to parental control. Id. at 351-52.
Similarly, in Littlejohn v. School Board of Leon
County, Florida , 132 F .4th 1232 (11th Cir. 2025), cert.
pending, No. 25-259, the Eleventh Circuit also assumed
that parents had standing to bring their claim. Once
again, the circuit court ruled against the parents, this
time imposing the overly burdensome “shocks the
conscience” test to deny parents the right to know about
their children’s gender transitions. Id. at 1245.
Recently, the Southern District of California reached
the merits of a claim for parents’ rights to know about, and

6
consent to, gender transitions and finally recognized that
such policies barring or preventing parental consent are a
blatant usurpation of parental authority. 2 In Mirabelli v.
Olson, the district court granted a preliminary injunction
for parents challenging “parental exclusion policies” that
required public school officials to withhold information
from parents concerning their child’s “gender expression.”
No. 3:23-cv-768-BEN-WVG, 2025 WL 3713588, at *3-4,
*28 (S.D. Cal. Dec. 22, 2025). The court held that such
policies harm children and teachers and violate parents’
rights to care, guide, and make healthcare decisions for
their children. Id. at *27. The court also found a violation
of parents’ right to train their children in their religious
beliefs. Id.; Id. at *17 (citing Mahmoud v. Taylor , 145
S. Ct. 2332 (2025)). Later, the court ruled explicitly that
the parents in the lawsuit had standing to challenge the
school policies. Mirabelli v. Olson , 761 F . Supp. 3d 1317,
1325-26 (S.D. Cal. 2025) (Jan. 7, 2025 Order Denying
Defendants’ Motions to Dismiss).
This Court should grant certiorari  in this case to
resolve the lower courts’ disagreement on whether parents
have standing to challenge governmental policies that
transition the genders of their children without their
2. Additionally, the United States Department of Education
Student Privacy Policy Office recently found that such policies
violate the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act. U.S.

Education Violated Federal Law by Hiding Students’ “Gender

us-department-of-education-finds-california-departmentof-education-violated-federal-law-hiding-students-gendertransitions-parents .

7
consent. Until this Court decides to offer some muchneeded clarity on this issue, the torturous story of Amica
Erin Lee will become more and more commonplace.
II.  Mrs. Lee is a victim of state-sponsored gender
ideology in violation of her parental rights,
demonstrating the need for the Court to affirm
parental standing to vindicate her rights and those
of the Plaintiffs in this case.
The story of Mrs. Lee is truly “troubling—and
tragic.” Lee v. Poudre Sch. Dist. R-1, 146 S. Ct. 26 (2025)
(Alito, J., concurring in denial of certiorari ). Mrs. Lee’s
daughter attended public school in the Poudre School
District (PSD) in Colorado and was directly impacted by
radical gender ideology policies promoted by her school.
Mrs. Lee’s daughter was first introduced to concepts of
gender fluidity and various types of sexual attraction at a
meeting of the school-sponsored, after-school organization
called Genders and Sexualities Alliance (GSA). Complaint,
Doc. 1, ¶ 28, Lee v. Poudre Sch. Dist. R-1 , No. 1:23-cv-
01117-NYW-STV (D. Colo., filed May 3, 2023). Mrs. Lee
was not made aware of the content of GSA’s activities by
the school, and school officials actively encouraged Mrs.
Lee’s daughter to keep the topics broached at the GSA
meeting a secret. Id. at ¶ 32. They even suggested that her
parents and home may not be a safe space for discussion
of these topics. Id.
When Mrs. Lee’s daughter was 12 years old, she
was a new student at Wellington Middle School (WMS),
struggling to adjust due to government shutdowns that
made classes remote. Id. at ¶¶ 35-38. In the spring of 2021,
her homeroom teacher, Jenna Riep, the staff sponsor of

8
the GSA club, personally invited Mrs. Lee’s daughter to
a GSA club meeting, falsely describing it as a “GSA Art
Club.” Id. at ¶ 42. This was an outright fabrication as there
is no evidence GSA has or ever had any art clubs. Id. at
¶¶ 40-43. Ms. Riep also failed to explain the meaning of
the acronym “GSA” to Mrs. Lee’s daughter, keeping Mrs.
Lee in the dark on the true nature of the organization. Id.
at ¶ 44. Nor was Mrs. Lee provided with notice of GSA’s
activities, agenda, or materials. Id. at ¶ 76.
Unaware of the meeting’s agenda, Mrs. Lee initially
permitted and even encouraged her daughter to attend the
meeting, seeing it as a way for her daughter to cultivate her
artistic talents, make friends, and become involved in the
school. Id. at ¶¶ 48-49. Unbeknownst to Mrs. Lee, however,
the GSA meeting hosted a guest speaker, Kimberly
Chambers, who was a part-time teacher with PSD and
ran an organization called Supporting Pride Learning and
Social Happenings (SPLASH). SPLASH educates school
aged children on topics of sexuality and gender identity.
Id. at ¶¶ 49-50. As it did for all guest speakers at schoolsponsored clubs at WMS, PSD approved Ms. Chambers
to speak. Id. at ¶ 51.
At the GSA meeting, Ms. Chambers told Mrs. Lee’s
daughter and the other children present that if they were
not completely comfortable in their bodies, that meant
that they were transgender. Id. at ¶ 54. Ms. Chambers
then proceeded to discuss with the children what sex
or gender they were attracted to. Id. at ¶ 55. Any child
who identified as transgender was awarded with LGBT
paraphernalia, including toys, flags, and other swag. Id. at
¶ 56. Thanks to a mixture of peer-pressure and a desire to
receive Ms. Chambers’ praise and prizes, several students

9
declared themselves to be transgender, including Mrs.
Lee’s daughter. Id. at ¶ 57.
Throughout the meeting, Ms. Chambers repeatedly
said that it may not be safe for the children to divulge the
discussions they had to their parents but that they would
be safe to discuss any of the subjects with Ms. Chambers
or Ms. Riep. Id. at ¶ 58. Ms. Chambers even went so far as
to hand out her personal phone number to the children and
invited them to connect with her on Discord. Id. at ¶¶ 59,
61. Ultimately at the GSA meeting, Mrs. Lee’s daughter
and the other children were “educated” on polyamory,
suicide, puberty blockers, sexualities, gender identities,
transgenderism, and changing names and pronouns,
despite the fact that Mrs. Lee had been informed they
were attending an art class. Id. at ¶ 60. Indeed, no artrelated activities were undertaken at any point during the
GSA meeting. Id. at ¶ 64.
After returning home from the GSA meeting, Mrs.
Lee’s daughter announced to Mrs. Lee that she would be
transitioning her gender. Id. at ¶ 66. This was the first time
that she had thoughts about transgenderism or expressed
any form of gender confusion to her parents. Id. Mrs. Lee’s
daughter also informed her parents that she had been
advised to keep secret from them the subjects discussed
at the GSA meeting. Id. at ¶ 69. Mrs. Lee and her husband
immediately disenrolled their daughter from WMS and
moved her to a private school. Id. But the damage to her
daughter and her family had been done.
Mrs. Lee’s daughter’s impromptu announcement
heavily impacted her relationship with her parents,
especially her father, and for several weeks they found

10
it difficult to communicate with one another. Id. at ¶ 70.
After disenrolling their daughter from WMS, Mrs. Lee
and her husband made a concerted effort to speak with
WMS principal Kelby Benedict. Id. at ¶ 71. Mr. Benedict
eventually acquiesced but insisted on meeting the Lees
at their home. Id. at ¶ 72. Mrs. Lee and her husband
would later learn that Mr. Benedict’s visit to their home
was, in fact, a de facto wellness check. Id. at ¶ 73. WMS
staffers had considered seeking a child protective services
wellness check for Mrs. Lee’s daughter after she was
disenrolled from WMS, and Mr. Benedict’s visit provided
an alternative wellness check. Id. During the course of
the Lees’ meeting with Mr. Benedict, he confirmed that
GSA clubs promote secrecy to create a “safe space” for
students. Id. at ¶ 74.
Far from making her feel safe, the GSA meeting
led Mrs. Lee’s daughter to experience a months-long,
downward spiral, including emotional decline, gender
and sexual confusion, and suicidal thoughts. Mrs.
Lee’s daughter would eventually require professional
counseling. Id. at ¶ 75.
Mrs. Lee’s traumatic experiences with PSD
demonstrate how intrusive radical gender ideology policies
and laws wrongfully interfere with parental rights. Not
only was PSD content to drive a wedge between Mrs.
Lee and her daughter while at WMS, but it also secondguessed Mrs. Lee’s decision to act in accordance with
what she thought was best for her daughter by removing
her from WMS.
If this Court continues to allow lower courts to ignore
this issue of great and growing national importance by

11
denying parents standing to bring similar claims, then
it will only help to create more victims like Mrs. Lee in
the future.
III. This case is well-suited to decide the question
whether parents have standing to challenge gender
transition policies without parental consent.
Unlike Parents Protecting Our Children, UA v. Eau
Claire Area School District , this is not a case in which
the parents have no connection to the policy at hand. 95
F .4th 501, 505 (7th Cir. 2024) (“nowhere does the complaint
allege that even one of the association’s members—any
particular parent—has experienced an actual or imminent
injury attributable to the Administrative Guidance or a
Support Plan”).
In the case now before the Court, one set of parents
has a gender confused child who has run away once and
may do so again. Pet. App. 77a. If and when the child does,
he will be exposed to the Washington law that genderconfused runaway minors must receive “gender affirming
treatment,” irrespective of parental consent. Wash. Rev.
Code § 13.32A.082(2)(c)(ii)-(d) (2023).
In addition, three other sets of parents also have
children who struggle with gender confusion, and these
parents vehemently oppose allowing their children to
transition. Pet. App. 70a, 72a, 73a. Two of these sets of
parents have been threatened that their children will be
taken away from them and forced to transition genders
without their consent. Pet. App. 72a, 74a-75a.

12
If the organization representing these parents does
not satisfy the standard for establishing associational
standing, then it is hard to imagine what organization
would. The Court should take this case to avoid even
more parents being subjected to the atrocities that these
parents—and Erin Lee—suffered.
CONCLUSION
For the foregoing reasons, amica curiae respectfully
requests that this Court grant certiorari  in this case.
Respectfully submitted,
